newsitem.title: FRANCE: SOCCER-LAMA FACING BAN, GARCION SUSPENDED OVER DRUGS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-LAMA FACING BAN, GARCION SUSPENDED OVER DRUGS.

text.p: French soccer was rocked by two drug scandals on Friday -- international goalkeeper Bernard Lama faced a two-month ban and Lille midfielder David Garcion was suspended for 18 months.
Lama was under threat of a two-month suspension after testing positive for cannabis but he said he had asked for the second analysis to be undertaken.

"The procedure is going on and I won't make any comment before it is completed. Everything has not been done according to the rules so far and I wish for the procedure to be respected," Lama told reporters.
Normal doping control procedures state that no statement should be made public before the second sample was tested.
But unsourced reports of positive dope tests have repeatedly leaked in recent months, especially in cycling, before the whole procedure had been completed.
"There won't be any statement, neither from me nor from my Paris St Germain club and I don't have to tell you when the second test will take place," Lama added.
If the second examination confirms the first, Lama would be sidelined for two months.

Lille club sources said Garcion had been banned for 18 months by the French soccer federation after testing positive for steroids. It was the longest suspension ever imposed on a French soccer player for doping.
The sources said he failed a dope test at the end of a league match between Nice and Lille on December 20. A second test confirmed traces of steroids in the player's urine.
"I will defend my case in due course. But I feel relieved that this case is revealed to the public," Garcion said.
The midfielder said he had been unaware of being given the steroids and that he had been surprised when failing the test.
The commission of appeal must hear the case within six months following the test which means it will meet before June 20.
Lille president Bernard Lecomte said he would "stand by his player".
"He is a balanced boy, everybody's fond of him. I can't believe he took such products, the more so as steroids are useless in football," he said.
According to press reports, Lama failed a dope test during training with the French squad for a friendly against the Netherlands in February.
Lama, capped 35 times by France, was not included by manager Aime Jacquet in the team who beat Sweden 1-0 on Wednesday. He was replaced by Monaco's Fabien Barthez.
Ironically, Barthez was the first top French player to be banned for taking cannabis after testing positive in October 1995. He was suspended for two months.
Since then a number of first division players, including former Paris St Germain defender Oumar Dieng and former international Stephane Paille have also received similar bans for smoking cannabis.
If he is banned, Lama could miss the Tournoi de France in June, a dress rehearsal for the 1998 World Cup, involving Italy, Brazil and England.
